summary: Validated the 'included' filter on /api/admin/catalog and /api/admin/catalog/discover. Only devices whose tuya_id appears in local_devices with included=True are exposed. All 6 backend tests pass (auth regression + catalog filter + toggle + discover + QR format).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1695 lines — consider splitting into modules (catalog, auth, installations, tuya) for maintainability.
included_local_ids() runs on every /admin/catalog and /admin/catalog/discover call; fine for now but consider indexing local_devices.tuya_id if the collection grows.
The discover endpoint silently swallows non-TuyaError exceptions with a generic 'connexion impossible' — logging the actual exception would help future debugging.
test_credentials: super_admin admin@climazone.fr / Admin1234! — login returns access_token
seed_data_creation: Seeded 3 catalog rows (TSTINC001 included, TSTEXC002 excluded, TSTNOL003 no local_device entry) + 2 local_devices; auto-cleaned in teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run test_catalog_included_filter.py serially (or via xdist_group='catalog_serial'). Parallel workers share MongoDB and race on the seed fixture. discover endpoint may return status 200 with empty items + errors (Tuya cloud unreachable / IP not whitelisted) — that is acceptable; the filter still holds.
rca of the issue: Bug reported: catalog QR tab showed all Tuya devices, including personal/non-system ones. Fix in server.py lines 960-970 introduced included_local_ids() and filters both /api/admin/catalog and /api/admin/catalog/discover with 'if c[tuya_id] in included'. Validated by seeding 3 catalog docs with different local_devices states and asserting only the included one appears; also validated by flipping included flags and re-querying. Regression on auth (/api/auth/login + /api/auth/me) also passes.
